official.status_note: The program announcement states the AEF Program is now open for applications and applications are due November 5, 2026 at 8:00pm ET.
benefits: Receives a monthly living stipend of $8,200.
Has a travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by their host agency; limitations on foreign travel vary by agency.
Has an education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved expenses aligned with the Fellow's individual professional development plan, including courses, conferences, and professional books.
Is reimbursed for moving/relocation expenses up to $3,500 for Fellows relocating from outside of the Washington, DC area.
Is eligible to receive a stipend of up to $550 per month (individual plan) or $1,300 per month (family plan) to offset the cost of health insurance.
Receives designated office space and agency/office-specific orientation and training, plus twice-monthly professional development meetings.
eligibility: Be a U.S. citizen at the time of applying (by the November 5, 2026 application deadline).
Have a minimum of five complete years of full-time classroom teaching experience prior to submitting the application; student teaching does not count toward this minimum.

Have been teaching full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school for at least five of the last seven years in a science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) discipline; current employment may be as an educator or district official.
Be currently employed full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school or school district in the U.S.
Be able to provide a letter of recommendation from a school district official as one of their three required letters of recommendation.
Be able to obtain a leave of absence from teaching in order to participate in the program for the full eleven months.
requirements: All applications must be completed online through the online application system; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for evaluation and placement.

Completion of all required fields: contact information; education background (formal and continuing education); teaching and professional experience; professional awards and recognition; citizenship status; interest in federal agency and/or Congressional office placement; and five essay questions.

Submission of three letters of recommendation online, including one recommendation letter from a school district official; school district officials do not include department chairs, assistant principals, associate principals or vice-principals.
Provide proof of U.S. citizenship upon accepting a Fellowship offer.
Complete the eleven-month full-time appointment in Washington, DC, beginning the third Monday in August with the initial program Orientation.
Have health care coverage during the fellowship appointment; Fellows are eligible to participate in the ORISE health insurance plan if they do not have other coverage.
documents: Completed online application with all required fields.
Three letters of recommendation submitted online, one of which must be from a school district official.
selection_criteria: Interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Program.

Sponsoring federal agencies review alignment of the applicant's experience and subject matter expertise with the host office, preparedness for the fellowship, and quality of recommendations before selecting semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC.
coverage: Travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency.
Education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved professional development expenses aligned with the Fellow's individual professional development plan.
Relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for Fellows relocating from outside of the Washington, DC area.
Health insurance stipend of up to $550 per month (individual plan) or $1,300 per month (family plan).
application_method: Create a new User ID and Password in the online application system ('Create New Account').
Complete all required fields, drafting the five essay responses offline in word processing software and pasting them into the online application.

Request recommendations from three individuals familiar with the applicant's professional and education background, including one school district official, via the Request Recommendations page; requests can be sent before the application is complete.
Monitor the 'Check Your Status' page to confirm all three recommendations have been submitted and use the 'Resend Email' button to chase recommenders.
Submit the completed application, including all three letters of recommendation, by 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026.
official.application_route: Apply online through the AEF online application system; every component, including all three recommendation letters, must be submitted through the system by 8:00pm ET on November 5, 2026.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be U.S. citizens at the time of applying (by the November 5, 2026 application deadline).
official.international_eligibility: No. The program FAQ confirms applicants must be U.S. citizens at the time of applying; a permanent resident who expects citizenship before the fellowship year is not eligible to apply.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Accomplished K-12 STEM educators; placements in participating federal agencies (Department of War, Department of Energy, Library of Congress, U.S. Geological Survey) or U.S. Congressional offices, with the DOE sponsoring up to five congressional office placements.
official.duration: Eleven months, mid-August through mid-July; the fellowship begins on the third Monday in August with the initial program Orientation.
official.description: The Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program gives accomplished K-12 STEM educators eleven months working in Federal agencies or U.S. Congressional offices, applying their classroom experience to national education program and/or education policy efforts. Managed by the DOE Office of Science's Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists with ORISE, it pairs a monthly living stipend with travel, education, relocation and health insurance allowances and access to a national network of education leaders and programs.

verification.notes: Stipend, allowances, deadline and eligibility verified on the DOE Office of Science AEF pages (Benefits, Key Dates, Eligibility, How to Apply, FAQ); the programme publishes no English test requirement and is not a degree award, so no tuition figure exists.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a stipended eleven-month policy fellowship, not a degree or a salaried job: you trade your classroom for a federal agency or congressional office in Washington, DC and draw a monthly living stipend. For the 2027-2028 cycle the window runs from August 3, 2026 to 8:00pm ET on November 5, 2026, and nothing counts unless the entire file, including all three recommendation letters, shows complete in the online system by that moment. Treat the $8,200 as gross pay: the programme withholds no tax and stipends are IRS-reportable, so plan quarterly estimated payments and DC-area housing costs, which the programme does not arrange.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Veteran U.S. public or private school STEM teachers with five-plus years of full-time classroom experience who can secure an eleven-month leave of absence and want a foothold in national education policy.
application_readiness_checklist: Create your online account early and confirm you actually meet the five-complete-years full-time teaching rule, excluding student teaching.
Line up a qualifying district-official recommender (principal, superintendent or board member level) well before November.
Draft and spell-check the five essays offline, since the system times out after 60 minutes of inactivity.
Send all three recommendation requests as soon as you have account access; they do not need to wait for your essay drafts.
Check the 'Check Your Status' page weekly and resend reminders until all three letters show submitted.
Block February 27 - March 1, 2027 now in case you are called to DC for semi-finalist interviews.
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete file at 8:00pm ET on November 5, 2026 because one recommendation letter never arrived through the system.
Choosing a district official who does not qualify: assistant, associate and vice-principals and department chairs are explicitly excluded.
Counting student teaching or assistant teaching toward the five-year classroom requirement.
Being currently employed outside a U.S. school or district, including teaching abroad.
Reapplying as a current or former AEF Fellow, or exceeding three applications in a six-year period.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Washington, DC housing (the programme provides resources but no housing), federal and state income tax with no withholding, health insurance above the $550/$1,300 monthly stipend amounts, and any family relocation costs beyond the $3,500 allowance.
document_audit: Recommendation letters are valid only if submitted through the online Recommender form; mailed or emailed letters are refused and a submitted letter cannot be removed.
Citizenship proof is required only when you accept an offer, so applicants in naturalisation should note the FAQ bar on applying before citizenship.
The five essays must be pasted into the online application fields; there is no separate document upload route for them.
alerts: U.S. citizenship must already be held at the time of applying, not by the fellowship start date.
The deadline is 8:00pm Eastern, not midnight Pacific; build in recommenders' time zones.
If selected for a congressional placement you must return to DC for a week of interviews in mid-June 2027.
Stipends are paid semi-monthly by the sponsoring agency and are reportable to the IRS with no withholding.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account, complete all fields and five essays, trigger the three online recommendation requests, monitor 'Check Your Status' until every letter is received, then submit before the 8:00pm ET deadline.

official.application_cycle: 2026 Solicitation 2; 2027 Solicitation 1 dates are published but marked tentative (application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027)
official.status_note: The program announcement states SCGSR is now open for applications and applications are due November 4, 2026, at 5:00PM ET; the online application system closes at that time and no additional materials are accepted.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award does not pay tuition or fees: the awardee and their graduate thesis advisor are responsible for any tuition or fees required by the graduate institution for the awardee to remain enrolled during the award term.
official.funding_period: per month while at the host laboratory
benefits: Living stipend: a monthly stipend in the amount of up to $3,600 for general living expenses while at the host DOE laboratory/facility during the award period.

Inbound and outbound transportation reimbursement, limited to a total travel benefit of up to $3,000 per award, available only if the host DOE national laboratory/facility is greater than 50 miles from the awardee's home graduate institution.
Supplemental awards are intended to cover incremental costs associated with living and travel expenses during the award period.
Option to apply, only after receiving the SCGSR award, for further funding to conduct a brief (6 weeks maximum) research visit to select research institutions abroad such as CERN or RIKEN.
The program does not provide additional support for supplies, materials, or travel while conducting the SCGSR research project at the host DOE laboratory/facility.
eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and be at least 18 years of age.

Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a Qualified Graduate Program with the Ph.D. as their degree objective, and at the time of application must have obtained Ph.D. candidacy with an established, defined graduate thesis project and graduate thesis advisor.

Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. in physics, chemistry, material sciences, geosciences, biology (non-medical), mathematics, engineering, computer or computational sciences, or select areas of environmental sciences aligned with the DOE Office of Science, at an accredited college or university in the United States or its territories.
The graduate thesis research must be in an area of fundamental research aligned with the DOE Office of Science Priority Research Areas identified for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2.

The applicant and their primary graduate thesis advisor are responsible for identifying a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist and jointly developing the research proposal; the proposed research at the laboratory may range from 3 to 12 consecutive months.

Applicants must remain enrolled as full-time graduate students during the project period; joint BS/MS, DVM, MBA, MD, joint MD/PhD, JD and joint JD/PhD degree programs and the social sciences are not eligible.
requirements: All applications must be completed through the online application system; only complete applications submitted by the deadline will be considered for review.

Complete all required fields: contact information; academic information including current graduate program information; citizenship or permanent residency status; professional information such as scientific publications and awards; graduate thesis advisor and collaborating DOE laboratory scientist contact information.
Submit the SCGSR research proposal, co-developed with the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist in consultation with the primary graduate thesis advisor, as a PDF through the online application.

Upload a PDF copy of current official graduate transcripts with all Social Security numbers and/or dates of birth redacted; applications containing unredacted PII are deemed non-compliant and will not be considered.

Provide official proof of Ph.D. candidacy: a signed letter from the university/college Registrar's office or the Chair, Head or Director of Graduate Studies, certifying completion of all required coursework and a thesis topic approved by the thesis committee with the approval date.
Submit two Letters of Support through the online system, one from the primary graduate thesis advisor and one from the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist, both received before the deadline.
documents: Completed online application with all required fields.
SCGSR research proposal (PDF), co-developed with the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist.
Official graduate transcripts (PDF) with Social Security numbers and dates of birth redacted.
Official proof of Ph.D. candidacy (signed letter from the Registrar or Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies).
Two Letters of Support (primary graduate thesis advisor and collaborating DOE laboratory scientist) submitted through the online system.
Citations of publications and awards, no more than 3 for each, entered in the online application.
selection_criteria: Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research: whether the research is well-conceived, the method and approach appropriate, the student sufficiently prepared, and DOE laboratory resources adequate.

Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training: whether the research makes a significant contribution to the thesis project and enhances graduate training and research skills.
Eligibility and compliance review first, then external merit review by subject matter experts using DOE Office of Science standard merit review processes.
Selection also reflects other program policy factors, including availability of funds and balance of portfolio.
coverage: Monthly stipend of up to $3,600 for general living expenses while at the host DOE laboratory/facility.
Inbound and outbound transportation reimbursement up to a total of $3,000 per award, only if the host laboratory is more than 50 miles from the home graduate institution.
The award does not pay tuition or fees; the awardee and their graduate thesis advisor remain responsible for tuition and fees required to remain enrolled.
No support for supplies, materials, or travel while conducting the SCGSR research project at the host laboratory.
application_method: Create an account on the SCGSR online application system well before the deadline and become familiar with the information requested.
Identify a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist (the SCGSR Program Manager can recommend candidates) and co-develop the research proposal with them in consultation with your thesis advisor.
Upload the research proposal PDF, official graduate transcripts with PII redacted, and official proof of Ph.D. candidacy.
Enter the thesis advisor and collaborating scientist contact information and send the two Letters of Support requests through the online system; monitor receipt and remind them as needed.
Review and print or export the application via 'Print your Application', then submit and confirm the Status page shows 'Submitted' before 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026.
official.application_route: Apply online through the SCGSR online application system; the proposal, transcripts, candidacy proof and both letters of support must all be in the system by 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026.
official.study_mode: full-time at the host laboratory while remaining enrolled full-time at the home institution
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be U.S. Citizens or Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR) at the time of application and at least 18 years of age.
official.international_eligibility: No for foreign students on an F-1 visa. U.S. citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents are eligible, but LPRs are encouraged to contact the host laboratory early about foreign-national site access lead times, since offers depend on lab approval.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Thesis research must align with a DOE Office of Science priority research area for the 2026 SCGSR Solicitation 2, and the host must be a participating DOE national laboratory or user facility; for BES priority areas, eligibility also depends on proximity between the applicant's university and the host laboratory.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal co-developed with the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist is required from all applicants; it must address the stated aims of at least one SCGSR Priority Research Area and identify how the host laboratory's capabilities and assets will be used, and must be an integral part of the doctoral thesis approved by the thesis advisor.
official.duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months at the DOE laboratory/facility; for 2026 Solicitation 2, project periods may start as early as June 7, 2027 and must start no later than October 4, 2027.
official.description: The Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) program provides supplemental awards so thesis-based U.S. doctoral students can conduct part of their dissertation research at a DOE national laboratory or facility, collaborating with a DOE laboratory scientist in an Office of Science priority research area. Awardees receive a monthly stipend of up to $3,600 and up to $3,000 of inbound/outbound travel reimbursement, while remaining full-time students and guest scientists, not employees, at the host laboratory.
official.program_type: Government supplemental research award for PhD students

verification.notes: Stipend cap, travel benefit, deadline and eligibility verified on the DOE Office of Science SCGSR pages (Benefits, Key Dates, Eligibility, How to Apply, FAQ); no English test requirement is published on the official site.

applicant_utility.summary: SCGSR supplements your existing PhD support rather than replacing it: it pays up to $3,600 a month while you spend 3 to 12 months doing part of your thesis at a DOE lab, but you keep paying your own tuition, arrange your own housing, and buy your own supplies. The 2026 Solicitation 2 deadline is 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026, and the real work is upstream of the form, securing a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist and co-writing a proposal that fits a published priority research area. Because merit review is external and hinge on scientific merit plus relevance to your thesis, a thin or mismatched proposal fails even from an otherwise perfectly eligible applicant.
applicant_utility.best_fit: PhD candidates past candidacy in DOE-aligned STEM fields whose thesis genuinely needs a DOE lab's facilities and who can be away from campus full-time for a consecutive 3 to 12 month block.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact the SCGSR Program Manager (sc.scgsr@doe.gov) or a lab point of contact as early as possible if you have no collaborating scientist in mind.
Request the candidacy letter from the Registrar or Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies now, making sure it states the thesis committee approval date.
Order the official graduate transcript, then redact every Social Security number and date of birth while keeping your name visible.
Co-develop the three-page proposal with the lab scientist and circulate the final PDF to both them and your thesis advisor before upload, since the system notifies them of every update.
Send both Letters of Support requests through the system early and track receipt, since letters cannot be fixed after submission.
Attend an application assistance workshop (September 3 or October 1, 2026) or the Friday office hours to pressure-test your priority-area fit.
common_rejection_risks: Applying before achieving Ph.D. candidacy, or without a defined thesis topic approved by the thesis committee.
An unredacted Social Security number or date of birth on the transcript, which the program deems non-compliant outright.
A proposal that duplicates the scope of a previously awarded SCGSR application.
Being in an excluded programme: MD, MBA, JD, DVM, joint MD/PhD, joint JD/PhD, joint BS/MS, or the social sciences.
Currently conducting research at the same DOE lab you propose to visit, or a past collaboration there longer than three months.
Missing a letter of support because it was emailed instead of submitted through the online form.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and fees at your home institution, housing and daily living costs beyond the monthly stipend, research supplies and materials, any travel between the lab and your university during the project, and income tax on the stipend since DOE/ORISE does not withhold.
document_audit: The candidacy letter must be signed by the Registrar or the Chair/Head/Director of Graduate Studies; letters signed by administrative staff are not accepted, and it must certify both completed coursework and an approved thesis topic with its approval date.
Only official graduate transcripts stamped with the university seal are accepted; unofficial electronic copies are rejected, and undergraduate transcripts are not requested.
Both Letters of Support must arrive through the unique URLs the system emails to your recommenders; a letter cannot be deleted or replaced once submitted.
Supplemental materials such as publications are not reviewed; at most three citations each for publications and awards are listed in the application fields.
alerts: The system closes at exactly 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026, with no late materials accepted of any kind.
F-1 visa students are not eligible; LPRs should start foreign-national site access paperwork with the host lab during the application window.
You must work full-time at the host lab during normal business hours: regular commuting back to your university violates the award terms.
Accepting any separate paid position at the host lab, such as an intern role, voids SCGSR eligibility.
Cumulative SCGSR awards cannot exceed 12 months, and offers arrive April 1-16, 2027 with only about a week to decide.
For 2027 Solicitation 1 all dates are tentative (opens February 2027, due May 2027), so do not plan around them as firm.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account, co-develop and upload the proposal with the lab scientist, upload the sealed redacted transcript and candidacy proof, trigger both letter-of-support requests through the system, and submit with the Status page showing 'Submitted' before 5:00 PM ET.
